newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-March 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-March 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
** India must aim for capital account convertibility of the rupee by 2000, International Monetary Fund (IMF) executive director M.R. Sivaraman said on Thursday.

"By the year 2000 should be our target when most of the regulations we have should go," he told reporters in response to a question on the time by which he thought India should aim for total convertibility of the rupee.
Capital flows into emerging markets are estimated to total around $230 billion in 1997, the same level as in 1996, IMF's Sivaraman said.

** In a significant turnaround, Bata India Ltd. has come out of the red. From a net loss of 421.6 million rupees in 1995, the firm has shown a profit of 41.5 million rupees for the year ended December 1996, the daily Economic Times reports.
** Pharmaceutical firm Rhone-Poulenc (India) on Thursday said it will begin paying royalties to France's Rhone-Poulenc Rorer SA (RPR), its principal shareholder, from April 1, 1997.
The firm's board decided to pay royalty of three percent on domestic sales and five percent on export sales, the company said in a statement.
